A protective style that actually protects your hair.

Two-strand twists are one of the most versatile protective styles for natural hair. Done right, they give your hair a real break from heat, tension, and daily manipulation. Done wrong, they cause the exact damage they were supposed to prevent. At Jae Stylez in Stafford, twists are installed with clean parts, low tension at the base, and a takedown plan that keeps your hair intact when the style comes down. Serving Stafford, Sugar Land, Missouri City, Richmond, and Greater Houston.

THREE WAYS TO WEAR TWO-STRAND TWISTS
Which Twist Fits Your Hair Right Now?

Two-strand twists are not one style. Depending on your hair length, how long you want to wear the style, and how much manipulation you want to give up, the right install method changes. Here is how the three most-requested versions compare.

blocks.title: Natural Hair Twists
items: How it works: Your natural hair is sectioned and twisted in two strands. No hair added.
Best for: Clients with enough length to hold a twist, quick installs, brides for makeup prep, protective wear for 1 to 2 weeks.
How long it lasts: Roughly 1 to 2 weeks worn as-is, or a base for a twist-out.
Trade-off: Twists can loosen faster than styles with added hair. Ends need to be secured.

blocks.title: Twists with Braided Base
items: How it works: Each twist starts with a small braid at the root, then transitions to two-strand for the length.
Best for: Clients who want twists to last longer, cleaner parts that hold up over the wear period, active lifestyles.
How long it lasts: Roughly 3 to 4 weeks with proper care.
Trade-off: Longer install time. Slightly higher tension at the root, which is why sizing matters.

blocks.title: Twists with Hair Added
items: How it works: Extensions are added at the root and twisted with your natural hair for length and thickness.
Best for: Clients wanting length beyond their own hair, longer wear time, low-maintenance protective style.
How long it lasts: Roughly 4 to 8 weeks depending on care and hair type.
Trade-off: Longer install, higher cost, more attention needed at the hairline to prevent tension damage.

blocks.text: SIZING
Small, Medium, or Large Twists?
Twist size affects how the style looks, how long it takes to install, how long it lasts, and how much stress it puts on your hair. Bigger is not always better.

blocks.title: Small Twists
items: Look: Delicate, high-definition, more styling versatility
Install time: 5 hours or longer
Wear time: Up to 6 to 8 weeks with hair added
Best for: Clients wanting maximum longevity, specific aesthetic goals, patient sitters

blocks.title: Medium Twists

Install time: 3 to 4 hours
Wear time: 3 to 6 weeks
Best for: First-time twist clients, most natural hair textures, everyday wear

blocks.title: Large Twists
items: Look: Bold, chunky, statement style
Install time: 2 to 3 hours
Wear time: 2 to 4 weeks
Best for: Short-term protective wear, thick natural density, clients who cannot sit long

blocks.title: How to Prep
items: Come with clean, product-free hair. Shampoo is included on natural hair services, but heavy oil or gel the day of slows the install.
Blowdry or stretch is not required. Hair gets stretched during sectioning.
If bringing your own hair for extensions, confirm brand and length at booking.
Eat before you come. Full installs run 3 to 6 hours.
Bring a snack, water, and something to watch.
Wear something you can sit in and skip anything that pulls over the head.

blocks.title: How to Wear It Right
items: Sleep on satin every night. Satin bonnet or satin pillowcase, not cotton.
Do not over-wash. Refresh every 2 to 3 weeks with a diluted shampoo or dry shampoo.
Mist with water and light oil at the scalp every 2 to 3 days.
Do not re-twist your own twists between visits. That is what unravels the install early.
Take the style down at week 4 to 6 for natural hair, week 6 to 8 for hair-added, whichever comes first. Do not push past 8 weeks.

items.q: How much do two-strand twists cost in Houston?
items.a: Two-strand twist pricing at Jae Stylez depends on twist size, whether hair is added, and length. Final pricing is confirmed at booking. Natural hair twists start lower than hair-added extension installs.

items.q: How long do two-strand twists last?
items.a: Natural hair twists last 1 to 2 weeks as-is. Twists with a braided base last 3 to 4 weeks. Twists with hair added last 4 to 8 weeks depending on twist size and care.

items.q: How long does the appointment take?
items.a: Natural hair twist installs run about 2 to 3 hours. Twists with braided base or hair added run 4 to 6 hours depending on size and length.

items.q: Can I wash my twists?
items.a: Yes, gently. Refresh every 2 to 3 weeks with a diluted shampoo. Avoid heavy scrubbing. Squeeze water through, do not rub. Air dry or sit under a hooded dryer.

items.q: Will two-strand twists damage my hair?
items.a: Not when installed with low tension and taken down on time. Damage happens when twists are too tight at the hairline or worn past 8 weeks and mat at the root.

items.q: What size twist should I get?
items.a: Small twists last longest and give the most versatility but take the longest to install. Medium is the balanced default. Large is fastest but wears out sooner. Density and lifestyle also affect the recommendation.

items.q: Can two-strand twists be worn as a twist-out?
items.a: Yes. Natural hair twists left in for 2 to 5 days and then unraveled give a defined twist-out. Slightly damp hair at install produces the best result.

items.q: Do you install twists on kids?
items.a: Yes. Twist services are offered for children with age-appropriate sizing and gentler tension at the hairline. Bring a snack and something for them to watch.

items.q: Do you use my own hair for extensions or do you provide it?
items.a: Clients bring their own hair for extension services. Recommendations on brand, texture, and quantity are given at booking so you buy the right amount.

items.q: Can I get twists on relaxed hair?
items.a: Twists work best on natural or transitioning hair. Relaxed hair holds twists but wears out faster and can loosen at the base sooner.

items.q: How do I take twists down without damage?
items.a: Saturate hair with water and conditioner, unravel each twist gently from ends to root, detangle in sections, then wash and deep condition immediately. Do not comb through dry twists.

items.q: What is the difference between two-strand twists and Marley twists?
items.a: Two-strand twists are the technique, using two sections of hair twisted around each other. Marley twists refers to the Marley hair extensions often added for a specific textured look. Same technique, different hair.

INSTANT OR STARTER LOCS
Two Ways to Begin. They Are Not the Same.
The name is close, but the process, the wait, and the result on install day are completely different. Here is how to know which one fits what you actually want.

blocks.title: Instant Locs
items: How it works: Crochet method builds a fully-locked loc during the install. Each loc is compressed and secured on day one.
What you leave with: Mature-looking locs immediately. No unraveling risk, no budding phase.
Timeline to "settled": Roughly 4 to 8 weeks for locs to relax and fully integrate with your natural texture.
First maintenance: 6 to 10 weeks after install.
Best for: Clients who cannot commit to the starter loc journey, transitioning natural hair, quick conversions.
Trade-off: Higher install price. Crochet locs can feel dense or firm for the first few weeks before they soften.

blocks.title: Starter Locs
items: How it works: Two-strand, comb coil, or interlocking method starts locs and lets them mature over months.
What you leave with: Twists, coils, or freshly interlocked sections. Not yet locked.
Timeline to "settled": 4 to 12 months depending on method and hair texture.
First maintenance: 4 to 6 weeks after install.
Best for: Clients who want to watch their locs develop, natural texture at every stage, lower upfront cost.
Trade-off: Requires patience through the budding phase. Higher risk of unraveling in the first few washes.

blocks.text: WHO INSTANT LOCS ARE FOR

blocks.title: Instant Locs Work Best For
items: Clients who want mature-looking locs on install day.
Natural hair that is at least 3 to 4 inches long.
Transitioning clients who do not want to big chop first.
Anyone with a work schedule, travel plans, or events that make a 6 to 12 month starter journey impractical.
Clients converting from twists, braids, or short natural styles.
Fine or thin hair textures that struggle to lock with palm rolling.

blocks.title: When to Choose Starter Locs Instead
items: You want to watch your locs develop from twist to mature.
You prefer a softer, more natural texture from day one.
You want the lowest upfront cost and are okay with the wait.
You have very short hair (under 2 inches) that comb coils would suit better.
You are undecided on committing to locs long term. Starter locs are easier to reverse in the first few months.

items.q: What are instant locs?
items.a: Instant locs are locs installed using the crochet method, which compresses and locks each section fully during the appointment. You leave with mature-looking locs the same day instead of waiting 6 to 12 months for starter locs to lock.

items.q: How long does the instant loc appointment take?
items.a: Full head instant loc installs run 4 to 6 hours depending on length and density. Partial installs run about 3 hours.

items.q: How much do instant locs cost at Jae Stylez?
items.a: Instant loc pricing depends on length, density, and size. Final pricing is confirmed at booking or consultation. Instant locs are priced higher than starter locs because the install builds the entire loc structure on day one.

items.q: Can I wash instant locs right after install?
items.a: Wait one week before the first wash. After that, wash gently every 1 to 2 weeks with a residue-free shampoo diluted in a bottle. Do not rub or scrub.

items.q: Do instant locs look different from starter or traditional locs?
items.a: On install day, yes. Instant locs already have shape and density. Over 6 to 12 months, they soften and blend into a texture that reads the same as any other mature loc.

items.q: How often do instant locs need maintenance?
items.a: First maintenance visit at 6 to 10 weeks. Regular maintenance every 8 to 10 weeks after that. Interlocking or crochet retwist depending on how the locs were installed.

items.q: Can I get instant locs on short hair?
items.a: Yes, as long as you have at least 3 to 4 inches of natural hair. Shorter than that and comb coils or a starter method may be a better fit.

items.q: Will instant locs damage my hair?
items.a: Not when installed and maintained by a stylist who knows the crochet method. Damage happens when locs are compressed too tightly, retwisted too often, or maintained with the wrong technique for the install type.

items.q: How long do instant locs last?
items.a: Locs are permanent once mature. Instant locs last as long as you want to keep them, with maintenance every 6 to 10 weeks.

items.q: Can instant locs be reversed?
items.a: Very difficult once mature. Instant locs are locked from day one, so the loc structure sets faster than starter locs. Comb-out or takedown becomes impractical after the first few months. Commit intentionally.

items.q: What is the difference between instant locs and loc extensions?
items.a: Instant locs use your own hair, compressed and locked. Loc extensions add pre-made or installed loc lengths to your natural hair for extra length or thickness. Both use the crochet method.

items.q: Do you install instant locs for men?
items.a: Yes. Instant loc services are offered for all clients regardless of gender. Same method, same pricing structure by length.

Clean parts, neat roots, and no tension at the base. Tight isn't the goal, locs that still have hair in them five years from now is. Whether your locs are established, brand new to us, or transferring from another stylist, you're welcome here. PALM ROLL OR INTERLOCKING
Two Ways to Maintain Locs. They Are Not Interchangeable.

Both close the new growth at the root. They differ in how long the retwist holds, how it wears over time, and how hard it is to reverse. Most clients do best with palm rolling. Active clients, fine hair, or anyone who can't get in every month often do better with interlocking. If you're unsure, book the consultation, it's cheaper than switching methods later.

blocks.title: Palm Roll
items: How it works: New growth is twisted and rolled so it wraps around the existing loc.
How long it holds: Roughly 4–6 weeks. Loosens sooner with sweat, swimming, or frequent washing.
Look: The classic smooth, cylindrical root most people picture with locs.
Best for: Clients on a regular schedule who like a polished, freshly-done root.
Trade-off: Doesn't hold as long, and over-twisting between visits is what thins roots.

blocks.title: Interlocking
items: How it works: The loc is pulled through its own root, locking new growth in place.
How long it holds: Roughly 6–10 weeks. Survives washing, swimming, and workouts.
Look: A slightly more textured root than palm rolling, with a visible grid at the base.
Best for: Active lifestyles, fine or thin hair, and anyone who can't get in every month.
Trade-off: Harder to reverse and unforgiving if done wrong — this one is worth paying for.

blocks.text: WHEN TO BOOK

blocks.title: Signs You're Due for a Retwist
items: New growth at the root is starting to marry two locs together.
Parts are hard to separate without pulling.
Roots look puffy or undefined and won't lie in their sections.
Frizz at the base is outpacing what a mist or oil can smooth.
You have an event coming up and want a clean root that photographs well.
It's been four to six weeks since your last full retwist.

blocks.title: Gone Longer Than You Meant To?
items: Book it anyway. Going four or five months between retwists isn't a reason to avoid the salon, it's a reason to come in before locs start joining at the root, which turns a maintenance visit into a separation appointment.

If it's been a while, or your locs are matted, thinning, or breaking at the root, book the consultation first. Thirty minutes and a real plan beats guessing at a service that might not be the right one.

items.q: How much is a loc retwist in Houston?
items.a: At Jae Stylez in Stafford, a full palm roll retwist is $120 and takes about 90 minutes, with a shampoo included. A partial retwist is $80. Interlocking maintenance is $315. Prices reflect service time and technique, not a package upsell.

items.q: What is a partial retwist?
items.a: A partial retwist covers the perimeter and the parts that show — hairline, edges, and the top — instead of every loc. It's $80 and takes about an hour. Useful between full appointments or before an event, but it isn't a replacement for full maintenance.

items.q: How often should locs be retwisted?
items.a: Every four to six weeks for palm rolling and six to ten weeks for interlocking. Slower growth, larger locs, or thicker density can go longer. Retwisting more often than that thins the root over time.

items.q: Is a retwist the same as interlocking?
items.a: No. Palm rolling wraps new growth around the outside of the loc and holds four to six weeks. Interlocking pulls the loc through its own root and holds six to ten weeks. Interlocking is much harder to reverse and is best committed to intentionally, not as a one-off experiment.

items.q: Can retwisting thin my roots?
items.a: Yes, if it's done too tightly or too often. Traction at the base of the loc causes thinning and breakage, and severe cases don't grow back. A retwist should feel firm, never painful. If your last retwist gave you a headache or visible bumps, that's a red flag.

items.q: Can I book if another stylist did my locs?

items.q: What if it's been months since my last retwist?
items.a: Still book. Overdue roots take longer and may need separation work, so mention the timeframe when you book — that way enough time is set aside and we don't rush the visit.

THREE WAYS TO START LOCS
Pick the Start Method That Fits Your Hair

There is no one right way to start locs. There is a right way for your hair type, your lifestyle, and how patient you are with the "ugly phase." Here is how the three most common start methods compare, so you know what you are booking before you sit down.

blocks.title: Two-Strand Method
items: How it works: Hair is sectioned and twisted in two strands. Each twist becomes the base of a loc as new growth locks around it.
Best for: Type 4 hair, medium to thick density, clients who want a defined look from day one.
Locking timeline: Roughly 4 to 6 months to a mature loc, sometimes longer for finer hair.
Care in early months: Do not wash for the first two weeks. Retwist every 4 to 6 weeks.
Trade-off: Twists can unravel in the first few washes. Requires patience through the budding stage.

blocks.title: Comb Coil
items: How it works: Hair is coiled at the root with a fine-tooth comb, creating a tight spiral that locs as it grows.
Best for: Type 4 hair, shorter lengths (2 to 6 inches), clients wanting the smallest possible starter size.
Locking timeline: 6 to 12 months to a mature loc.
Care in early months: Coils are fragile at first. Sleep in a bonnet, avoid manipulation, retwist every 4 to 6 weeks.
Trade-off: Highest maintenance in the first 90 days. Coils can slip if hair is too fine or too silky.

blocks.title: Interlocking Start
items: How it works: New growth is pulled through the root, locking each section from the first appointment.
Best for: Fine hair, active lifestyles, clients who cannot commit to retwists every month, clients with textures that resist palm rolling.
Locking timeline: Locs are secure immediately. Full maturity in 4 to 8 months.
Care in early months: Wash freely after week 1. Interlocking maintenance every 6 to 10 weeks.
Trade-off: Harder to reverse. Requires a skilled hand to avoid thinning at the root.

Look: The middle ground most clients land on. Full without being heavy.
Maintenance: Standard retwist times, balanced density
Best for: Most clients starting locs for the first time

blocks.title: Large Locs
items: Count: Roughly 40 to 80 locs on a full head
Look: Bold, statement locs. Heavier feel once they grow.
Maintenance: Faster retwist times, fewer parts, lower price per visit
Best for: Clients with thicker density, low-maintenance preferences, or a specific mature-loc look in mind

items.q: How much do starter locs cost at Jae Stylez?
items.a: Starter locs start at $140 and go up based on size, density, and length. Final pricing is confirmed at the $30 consultation. Interlocking starts and longer two-strand installs are priced separately.

items.q: How long does the starter loc appointment take?
items.a: Full head installations run 3 to 5 hours depending on density and method. Two-strand starts on mid-back length hair can run longer. Eat before you come.

items.q: What is the best method to start locs?
items.a: There is no single best method. Two-strand is the softest start, comb coil is the traditional start, and interlocking is the longest-hold start. Method depends on hair type, texture, and lifestyle. A consultation confirms the fit before your install.

items.q: How long does it take for starter locs to lock?
items.a: Roughly 4 to 6 months for two-strand starts, 6 to 12 months for comb coils, and immediate hold with interlocking starts, with full maturity in 4 to 8 months. Growth rate, density, and hair texture all affect the timeline.

items.q: Can I wash my starter locs?
items.a: Not for the first two weeks. Washing too early is the most common reason starter locs unravel. After the first two weeks, wash gently with a residue-free shampoo every 1 to 2 weeks.

items.q: How often should I retwist starter locs?
items.a: Every 4 to 6 weeks for palm roll and two-strand starts. Every 6 to 10 weeks for interlocking. Retwisting more often than that thins the root before your locs even mature.

items.q: What size loc is best for me?
items.a: Small locs for maximum styling versatility, medium locs for balanced density (where most clients land), and large locs for bold, low-maintenance locs. Hair density and desired look are confirmed at the consultation before install.

items.q: Can I start locs if my hair is short?
items.a: Yes. Comb coils work well on 2 to 6 inch hair. Two-strand starts need enough length to hold a twist, usually 3 inches or more. Interlocking can start on very short hair with the right technique.

items.q: Do you start locs on all hair types?
items.a: Yes. Type 3 and Type 4 hair both loc. Finer textures may take longer to mature and often do best with interlocking to prevent slippage.

items.q: What if I already tried starting locs at home?
items.a: Bring them in for a consultation. Home starts can often be salvaged, evened out, or converted to a professional install without starting over.

items.q: Do you start locs for men?
items.a: Yes. Starter loc services are offered for all clients regardless of gender. Same pricing structure, same method options.

items.q: What is the difference between starter locs and instant locs?
items.a: Starter locs need time to mature into real locs (4 to 12 months depending on method). Instant locs use crochet or interlocking to lock the hair fully during the install, so you leave with mature-looking locs the same day.

blocks.text: SILK PRESS · STAFFORD, TX
Silk Press in Stafford, TX
A silk press your hair will still thank you for next month.

A silk press should look smooth on day one, move easily on day three, and still feel like your hair when wash day comes around. That means the right prep, the right heat, and enough time to actually finish the job. At Jae Stylez in Stafford, silk press appointments are built around hair health first. Correct products, protected roots, and a real conversation about what your hair can handle before we pick up the flat iron. Serving Stafford, Sugar Land, Missouri City, Richmond, and Greater Houston.

Two Ways to Get Smooth Hair. They Are Not the Same.
WHAT THE STYLE ACTUALLY IS

People say silk press and mean different things. Here is how a silk press compares to a traditional press or a heat-heavy blowout so you know what you are booking and what your hair should look like when you leave.

blocks.title: Silk Press
items: How it works: Hair is washed, deep conditioned, blown out with tension, and flat ironed in small sections at a controlled temperature.
Look: Sleek, smooth, natural movement. Bounce, not board-straight.
How long it lasts: 5 to 10 days depending on humidity, sleep habits, and workouts.
Best for: Natural hair in good condition, clients wanting a break from styling without giving up movement.
Trade-off: Requires precise heat control. Too hot and you damage the curl pattern.

blocks.title: Traditional Press or Heat-Heavy Blowout
items: How it works: Hair blown out at high heat and flat ironed at maximum temperature for maximum straightness.
Look: Board-straight, no movement, stiff.
How long it lasts: Falls flat or reverts within 2 to 3 days in humidity.
Best for: Nobody, in most cases. This is where heat damage starts.
Trade-off: Regular high-heat styling breaks down your curl pattern over time. Costs you your natural texture for a short-term result.

blocks.text: WHO SHOULD BOOK A SILK PRESS

blocks.title: Silk Press Works Best For
items: Natural hair in healthy, well-moisturized condition.
Clients wanting a break from daily styling without cutting or coloring.
Photo-ready styling for an event, wedding, or trip.
Length checks and end assessments before a trim.
Clients transitioning from relaxed to natural who want to see length without extensions.

blocks.title: When to Wait
items: Hair with recent heat damage or breakage. A silk press adds heat to already-stressed hair. Book a deep condition first.
Freshly colored hair that has not been evaluated. Chemical service plus heat too close together strains the strand.
Actively transitioning without a trim. Old chemically-treated ends do not press the same as new growth.
Clients wanting completely bone-straight, stiff hair. Silk press is smooth, not flat. That is the whole point.

blocks.text: WHAT THE APPOINTMENT LOOKS LIKE
Five Steps, No Surprises

items.label: Step 01
items.text: Consultation Hair condition, length, ends, and desired result. If a service is not the right fit today, you are told before we start.

items.label: Step 02
items.text: Shampoo Clarifying shampoo first when needed, followed by moisture shampoo. Product buildup is the fastest way to ruin a silk press before it starts.

items.label: Step 03
items.text: Deep Condition Every silk press includes a deep conditioner suited to your hair. Time under the dryer varies. Your hair tells us when it is ready.

items.label: Step 04
items.text: Blow Dry with Tension Sectioned blow dry with tension using a heat protectant. Hair is stretched, not fried, before the flat iron comes in.

items.label: Step 05
items.text: Flat Iron Small sections, controlled temperature, one to two passes per section. Overpassing is what damages hair. Precision saves your curl pattern.

items.q: How much does a silk press cost in Houston?
items.a: Silk press pricing at Jae Stylez depends on length, density, and add-ons. Final pricing is confirmed at booking or consultation. Longer than mid-back and add-ons like color or trim are priced separately.

items.q: How long does a silk press last?
items.a: Roughly 5 to 10 days depending on humidity, sleep habits, workouts, and your hair type. Wrapping at night and skipping day-one sweat extends the wear.

items.q: How long does the appointment take?
items.a: Standard silk press runs about 2 to 3 hours. Add a trim and it moves to 3 hours. Add a permanent color and it moves to 4 hours or more.

items.q: Will a silk press damage my natural hair?
items.a: Not when done at the right temperature with the right prep. Damage happens from too much heat, too many passes, or skipping deep condition. Getting silk pressed too often (more than once a month) also stresses the hair over time.

items.q: How often can I get a silk press?
items.a: Once a month or less is a safe cadence for most natural hair. More frequent than that and the cumulative heat starts breaking down the curl pattern. Space out silk presses with wash and gos, twist outs, or protective styles.

items.q: Can I wash a silk press to make it last longer?
items.a: No. Water reverts the style immediately. Use dry shampoo at the roots for oil control and wrap at night. When the press is done, wash and deep condition instead of adding more heat.

items.q: Can I get a silk press on transitioning hair?
items.a: Yes, with a consultation first. Transitioning hair often has weak zones where relaxed ends meet new growth. Silk pressing that zone requires careful heat and often a small trim.

items.q: Can I get a silk press on colored hair?
items.a: Yes, if the color is healthy. Recent bleach or repeated color plus regular silk pressing is risky. Book a consultation so we can look at your ends first.

items.q: Do you use heat protectant?
items.a: Every time. Heat protectant is not optional. Silk pressing without it is heat damage.

items.q: Should I get a trim with my silk press?
items.a: If it has been more than 3 months since your last trim, yes. Silk press shows every split end. Adding a small trim at the same appointment keeps the finish clean and protects your length over time.

items.q: What if my hair reverts fast because of humidity?
items.a: Houston humidity is real. A silk press in July lasts less than a silk press in December for most people. Wrapping at night and using an anti-humidity finishing spray helps. Do not add more heat to fix it.

items.q: Do you press hair for men?
items.a: Yes. Silk press services are offered for all clients regardless of gender. Same pricing structure by length.

blocks.text: GODDESS LOCS · STAFFORD, TX
Goddess Locs in Stafford, TX
Soft, textured, and unmistakably yours.

Goddess locs are the protective style you wear when you want length, softness, and a look that moves. Loose curly ends, boho detail woven through the length, and a finished install that feels light on the scalp. Done right, they protect your natural hair for weeks while giving you a style that photographs beautifully from every angle. At Jae Stylez in Stafford, goddess locs are installed with clean parts, low tension, and a takedown plan so your natural hair stays intact when the style comes down. Serving Stafford, Sugar Land, Missouri City, Richmond, and Greater Houston.
Goddess Loc Pricing

Goddess loc pricing depends on length, size, and how much boho detail you want woven through the install. Every appointment includes a consultation, clean sectioning, and a takedown recommendation so you know when to remove the style safely.
All services include a shampoo except braided styles. Deposits are non-refundable and applied to your service total.
Final pricing is confirmed at booking based on length, density, and hair added. Deposits are non-refundable and applied to your service total.
THREE VERSIONS OF THE LOOK
Goddess, Butterfly, or Faux? Choose the Finish.

Goddess locs is the umbrella. Underneath it are a few different install styles that all give you the boho, textured look but wear differently. Here is how the most-requested versions compare so you know which one you are actually booking.

blocks.title: Goddess Locs
items: How it works: Loose curly hair is wrapped around each loc extension, with curly ends left out for the signature boho finish.
Look: Soft, romantic, defined curls at the ends and throughout the length.
Wear time: Roughly 4 to 6 weeks with good care.
Best for: Clients wanting the traditional goddess loc aesthetic, defined curls, event-ready styles.
Trade-off: Curly ends need refreshing to stay defined. Not the lowest maintenance.

blocks.title: Butterfly Locs
items: How it works: Locs are installed and then intentionally distressed for a lived-in, textured look with visible loops throughout the length.
Look: Chunky, tousled, effortless. More texture, less curl.
Wear time: Roughly 4 to 6 weeks.
Best for: Clients wanting a low-effort daily style, edgy finish, less styling upkeep.
Trade-off: The distressed texture is a look. Not for clients who want clean, polished locs.

blocks.title: Faux Locs and Soft Locs
items: How it works: Locs are wrapped smooth and clean with less added texture. Knotless or invisible knot methods reduce bulk at the root.
Look: Sleeker, more uniform, closer to a mature loc appearance.
Wear time: Roughly 6 to 8 weeks.
Best for: Clients wanting length without a boho aesthetic, longer wear, cleaner finish.
Trade-off: Less "boho" feel. Requires precise install for the smoothest result.

blocks.text: SIZE AND LENGTH GUIDE

blocks.title: Small, Medium, or Large?
items: Small goddess locs: Delicate, more count per head, longest install time. Best for clients who want a natural-loc look at length.
Medium goddess locs: Balanced. Most-requested size. Balanced weight and definition.
Large goddess locs: Chunky, statement, fastest install. Best for shorter wear periods and clients who want minimal sit time.

blocks.title: Shoulder to Butt Length
items: Shoulder length: Lightest weight, most manageable daily wear, easiest to sleep in.
Mid-back: Most-requested length. Full drama without the full weight.
Butt length: Full commitment. Heaviest install, longest sit time, biggest visual impact. Plan the wear time accordingly.

blocks.title: How to Prep
items: Come with clean, product-free hair. Buildup and heavy oil slow the install.
Blowdry or stretch is not required. Hair is stretched during sectioning.
If bringing your own hair, confirm brand and quantity at booking. Recommendations given based on desired length and size.
Eat before you come. Full installs run 5 to 7 hours.
Bring snacks, water, and something to watch.
Wear something you can sit in and skip anything that pulls over the head.

blocks.title: How to Wear Them Right
items: Sleep on satin every night. Bonnet, scarf, or pillowcase, never cotton.
Refresh curly ends every 3 to 5 days with mousse or curl foam and a light spritz of water.
Wash gently every 2 to 3 weeks with diluted shampoo. Do not scrub the base.
Mist scalp with water and light oil every few days to keep natural hair moisturized.
Do not pull, restyle, or over-manipulate the ends. Distressed and curly finishes lose definition with too much touching.
Take the style down at week 6 to 8. Do not push past 8 weeks or matting starts at the root.

blocks.text: WHAT THE APPOINTMENT LOOKS LIKE
Five Steps, No Surprises

items.label: Step 01
items.text: Consultation Style choice (goddess, butterfly, faux, invisible), size, length, and desired finish confirmed before install.

items.label: Step 02
items.text: Shampoo Clean hair sets a clean install. Buildup or product residue addressed before we start.

items.label: Step 03
items.text: Section and Part Clean parts placed to sit flat under the install and grow out cleanly. Part placement determines how the style photographs and how it wears.

items.label: Step 04
items.text: Install Loc extensions installed using the method that matches your chosen style. Low tension at the hairline. Consistent size across the head.

items.label: Step 05
items.text: Finish Curly ends shaped, distressing done intentionally, aftercare walked through in real time. Take-down window discussed before you leave.

blocks.text: STRAIGHT TALK
What Ruins a Goddess Loc Install
These are the things that turn a beautiful protective style into a repair job.

items: Tension at the hairline. Goddess locs installed too tight around the edges cause traction and thinning. A loc should feel secure at the root, never painful.
Wearing past 8 weeks. After 8 weeks matting starts at the base and takedown becomes destructive. Book the takedown before you book the install.
Skipping moisture. Your natural hair still needs water and light oil under the style. Dry hair under a heavy install breaks at the root.
Restyling too aggressively. Constant pulling into buns or updos at the roots stresses the install and shortens wear time.
Wrong hair for the look. Cheap hair sheds, tangles, and reflects light like plastic. Better hair costs more up front but wears cleaner and photographs better.

items.q: How much do goddess locs cost in Houston?
items.a: Goddess loc pricing at Jae Stylez depends on length, size, and style variation (goddess, butterfly, faux, invisible). Final pricing is confirmed at booking based on the version you want and how much hair is being added.

items.q: How long do goddess locs last?
items.a: Roughly 4 to 6 weeks for classic goddess and butterfly locs, and 6 to 8 weeks for faux locs and soft locs. Do not wear past 8 weeks or matting starts at the base.

items.q: How long does the appointment take?
items.a: Full installs run 5 to 7 hours depending on length, size, and style. Butt-length installs run longer. Plan the day accordingly.

items.q: What is the difference between goddess locs and butterfly locs?
items.a: Goddess locs have wrapped locs with curly hair left loose along the length and at the ends. Butterfly locs are distressed intentionally for a chunky, textured, boho look with visible loops.

items.q: Are goddess locs a protective style?
items.a: Yes, when installed with low tension and taken down on time. They give your natural hair a break from daily manipulation and heat. Wearing them too long or installing them too tight causes the exact damage they were meant to prevent.

items.q: Can I wash goddess locs?
items.a: Yes, gently. Wash every 2 to 3 weeks with diluted shampoo. Do not scrub the base. Squeeze water through, air dry or sit under a hooded dryer.

items.q: Can I swim with goddess locs?
items.a: Yes with care. Wet your hair with fresh water before swimming, rinse thoroughly after, and dry fully. Chlorine and salt water break down the hair over time.

items.q: Do I bring my own hair?
items.a: Yes. Clients bring their own hair for install. Recommendations on brand, texture, and quantity are given at booking so you buy exactly what the style needs.

items.q: Will goddess locs damage my natural hair?
items.a: Not when installed correctly and taken down on time. Damage comes from tension at the hairline, wearing past 8 weeks, or aggressive takedowns.

items.q: What size goddess loc should I get?
items.a: Small locs for the most natural look and longest wear. Medium for balanced weight and the most-requested size. Large for statement styles and shorter installs.

items.q: How do I take goddess locs down without damage?
items.a: Cut the wrapped hair carefully section by section, saturate natural hair with water and conditioner, unravel gently from ends to root, then wash and deep condition immediately.

items.q: Do you install goddess locs on all hair textures?
items.a: Yes. Goddess locs work on Type 3 and Type 4 hair. Finer textures may need extra securing at the base. All confirmed at consultation.

blocks.text: MICROLOC EXTENSIONS · STAFFORD, TX
Microloc Extensions in Stafford, TX
Small locs, real length, from day one.

Microlocs give you a delicate, high-count loc look that traditional locs cannot match. Microloc extensions take that further by adding length at install, so you skip the years of waiting for microlocs to grow out. Each loc is installed individually using extension hair, matched to your texture, and secured with the same interlocking technique that keeps microlocs healthy long term. At Jae Stylez in Stafford, microloc extensions are installed with precision, low tension, and a maintenance plan built around retie cadence, not palm rolling. Serving Stafford, Sugar Land, Missouri City, Richmond, and Greater Houston.

WHAT MICROLOCS ACTUALLY ARE
Small Locs, High Count, Different Maintenance

Microlocs are locs installed at a smaller size than traditional locs, with a higher count per head. They read as delicate, versatile, and grown-in even at shorter lengths. What people miss is that microlocs are a different maintenance category. They are maintained with interlocking, not palm rolling, and they follow a longer retie schedule.

blocks.title: Microloc Extensions
items: How it works: Extension hair matched to your texture is installed loc by loc, adding both loc count and length in one appointment.
Best for: Clients who want microlocs but do not want to wait 2 to 3 years for length to grow out. Also for anyone starting the loc journey with shorter natural hair.
Maintenance: Interlocking retie every 6 to 10 weeks. Not palm rolled.
Trade-off: Highest install price, longest sit time. Extension hair still requires clean maintenance to blend seamlessly with new growth over time.

blocks.title: Microlocs Started from Your Own Hair
items: How it works: Twists, braids, or interlocks started at the root using only your natural hair.
Best for: Clients patient enough to grow microlocs from scratch and wanting a fully natural texture from the start.
Maintenance: Interlocking retie every 6 to 10 weeks after locking. Small palm rolling not recommended long term.
Trade-off: Longer wait for length. Full maturity takes 8 to 18 months depending on hair texture.

blocks.text: WHO MICROLOC EXTENSIONS WORK FOR

blocks.title: Microloc Extensions Are Best For
items: Clients wanting the delicate microloc look immediately, not in three years.
Fine or thin hair that struggles with traditional loc weight.
Clients transitioning from natural styles who want length without visible extensions.
Anyone whose lifestyle needs the longer retie window (interlocking every 6 to 10 weeks vs palm rolling every 4 to 6).
Loc clients wanting to change size or count without combing out and starting over.

blocks.title: When to Consider a Different Method
items: Clients who want mature locs same day without extensions (instant locs may be a better fit).
Clients hoping to grow their own hair to length rather than adding extension hair.
Very active clients who want the lowest possible maintenance cost per year. Microlocs cost more per install and per retie.
Clients unsure about the long-term commitment. Microlocs are difficult to reverse once mature.

blocks.title: Living With Microloc Extensions
items: Wash every 1 to 2 weeks with residue-free shampoo. Squeeze through, do not rub.
Sleep on satin every night. Cotton pulls at extension hair and thins natural hair at the base.
Do not palm roll your microlocs at home. They are interlocked, not palm rolled. Palm rolling on top of interlocking causes pilling and lumps.
Light hydration only. Water mist and a scalp oil. Skip beeswax and heavy grease.
Book retie at 6 to 10 weeks. Do not push past 12 weeks. Overdue microlocs mat at the base faster than traditional locs.

items.q: What are microloc extensions?
items.a: Microloc extensions are small locs installed with extension hair matched to your texture. You leave with microlocs plus length in one appointment instead of waiting 2 to 3 years for microlocs to grow out.

items.q: How much do microloc extensions cost?
items.a: Microloc extension pricing depends on loc count, extension hair length, and install time. Final pricing is confirmed at the $30 consultation. Reties are priced separately based on how many weeks since your last visit.

items.q: How long does the appointment take?
items.a: Full microloc extension installs vary widely by loc count. Plan for a full-day appointment (6 to 10 hours). Micro loc reties run 1 to 3 hours depending on how overdue you are.

items.q: Are microlocs the same as sisterlocks?
items.a: No. Sisterlocks is a trademarked system with proprietary tools, training, and a specific installation pattern. Microlocs is the general category of small locs, installed and maintained with interlocking. Both look similar. Different systems.

items.q: How often do microlocs need maintenance?
items.a: Retie every 6 to 10 weeks. Slower growth stretches the window. Do not push past 12 weeks or matting starts at the base.

items.q: Can I switch from traditional locs to microlocs?
items.a: Not directly. Traditional locs are too large to convert to microlocs. If you want microlocs, you either need to comb out and start over, or grow out and cut off traditional locs at a length you can transition from. A consultation confirms the right path.

items.q: Can microloc extensions be washed?
items.a: Yes, and they should be. Wash every 1 to 2 weeks with a residue-free shampoo diluted in a bottle. Do not rub or scrub.

items.q: Will microloc extensions damage my natural hair?
items.a: Not when installed and maintained correctly. Damage happens from tension at the base, wrong hair choices, or skipping retie appointments. A good install feels secure, never painful.

items.q: How long do microloc extensions last?
items.a: Locs are permanent once mature. The extension hair blends into your natural loc over time as new growth catches up. Most clients keep microlocs long term with regular maintenance.

items.q: What kind of hair is used for extensions?
items.a: Texture-matched loc hair from reputable brands. Recommendations are given at the consultation based on your hair and desired look. Cheap hair sheds and reads plastic. Better hair costs more up front and lasts longer.

items.q: Can I get microloc extensions on short hair?
items.a: Yes, with a consultation. Your natural hair needs enough length to hold the extension securely, usually 2 to 4 inches minimum. Very short hair may need to grow out first.

items.q: Do you install microlocs for men?
items.a: Yes. Microloc extension services are offered for all clients regardless of gender. Same install method, same maintenance schedule.

blocks.text: INTERLOCKING LOC MAINTENANCE · STAFFORD, TX
Interlocking Loc Maintenance in Stafford, TX
Longer hold. Fewer visits. Better for the hair that palm rolling wears out.

Interlocking is the loc maintenance method for people whose lives do not fit a four-week retwist schedule. Instead of wrapping new growth around the loc like palm rolling, each loc is pulled through its own root, locking new growth in place with a hold that survives washing, swimming, and workouts. Six to ten weeks between visits, not four to six. Better for fine hair. Better for anyone who has been told their edges cannot handle another tight retwist. At Jae Stylez in Stafford, interlocking is done with precision and low tension, so your locs get the hold without the thinning. Serving Stafford, Sugar Land, Missouri City, Richmond, and Greater Houston.
Interlocking Maintenance Pricing
Interlocking pricing depends on loc count, length, and how long it has been since your last visit. Every appointment includes a shampoo and a check for tension, breakage, or matting before we start.
All services include a shampoo except braided styles. Deposits are non-refundable and applied to your service total.
Final pricing is confirmed at booking based on loc count, length, and how long since your last visit. Deposits are non-refundable and applied to your service total.
Two Ways to Maintain Locs. This Is How They Actually Differ.
INTERLOCKING OR PALM ROLL

Interlocking and palm rolling both close new growth at the root. That is where the similarity ends. The right method depends on your hair type, your lifestyle, and honestly, how often you can realistically get in for maintenance.

blocks.title: Interlocking
items: How it works: Each loc is pulled through its own root using a small tool. New growth locks in place from the inside.
How long it holds: Roughly 6 to 10 weeks. Survives washing, sweat, and swimming without loosening.
Look: Slightly more textured root with a visible grid pattern at the base.
Best for: Fine or thin hair, active clients, anyone who cannot get in every month, clients with textures that resist palm rolling.
Trade-off: Harder to reverse. Unforgiving when done wrong. Higher price per visit but fewer visits per year.

blocks.title: Palm Roll
items: How it works: New growth is twisted and rolled so it wraps around the existing loc.
How long it holds: Roughly 4 to 6 weeks. Loosens faster with sweat, swimming, or frequent washing.
Look: Classic smooth cylindrical root.
Best for: Clients on a regular schedule who like a polished finish, most standard hair textures.
Trade-off: Requires more frequent visits. Over-retwisting between visits is the fastest way to thin roots.

blocks.text: WHO INTERLOCKING WORKS BEST FOR

blocks.title: When Interlocking Is the Right Answer
items: Fine or thinning hair that cannot handle regular palm rolling.
Active clients who swim, work out, or sweat regularly.
Clients traveling for work or living far from a loctician.
Clients coming out of tension damage who need a lower-manipulation option.
Clients with slippery textures where palm rolls unravel quickly.
Anyone tired of the 4-week retwist cycle.

blocks.title: When Palm Rolling Is Still Better
items: Locs that are already established with palm rolling and doing well. Switching methods is a big commitment.
Clients who love the polished palm roll finish and see their loctician regularly.
Very new locs still in the budding phase where the loc structure has not fully formed.
Clients who plan to comb out their locs one day. Interlocking makes reversing much harder.

blocks.text: WHAT THE APPOINTMENT LOOKS LIKE
Four Steps, No Surprises

items.label: Step 01
items.text: Check the Roots Every loc gets looked at before we start. Tension spots, breakage, matting, and slippage all get flagged so nothing gets worse during maintenance.

items.label: Step 02
items.text: Shampoo Clean locs interlock cleaner. Buildup or product residue is addressed first so the tool moves through the loc smoothly.

items.label: Step 03
items.text: Interlock Each loc pulled through its own root using a small precision tool. Consistent direction, consistent tension, no shortcuts. Direction gets rotated over visits so grid patterns do not become permanent.

items.label: Step 04
items.text: Dry and Set Fully dried before you leave. Aftercare walked through. Next visit scheduled at 6 to 10 weeks depending on your growth.

FAQs
Straight Answers

items.q: How much does interlocking maintenance cost?
items.a: Interlocking maintenance at Jae Stylez is $315 for a full head. Micro loc reties are priced separately based on how many weeks it has been since your last visit and how many locs are involved.

items.q: How long does interlocking maintenance last?
items.a: Roughly 6 to 10 weeks between visits. Slower growth can stretch that longer. Faster growth may need visits closer to the 6-week mark.

items.q: How is interlocking different from palm rolling?
items.a: Palm rolling wraps new growth around the outside of the loc. Interlocking pulls the loc through its own root, locking new growth from the inside. Interlocking holds longer, survives washing and workouts, and is much harder to reverse.

items.q: Can I switch from palm rolling to interlocking?
items.a: Yes, with a consultation first. Not every loc is a good candidate for switching, and doing it wrong can loosen or damage established locs. A consultation confirms whether your locs are ready.

items.q: Is interlocking the same as sisterlocks?
items.a: No. Sisterlocks is a specific trademarked system with proprietary tools and training. Interlocking is the general technique. Both use the same core method of pulling the loc through its own root.

items.q: Can interlocking damage my locs?
items.a: Yes, if done wrong. Interlocking in the same direction every visit creates a permanent grid pattern that weakens the loc. Too much tension causes thinning. A skilled stylist rotates direction and uses controlled tension.

items.q: How long does the appointment take?
items.a: Full head interlocking maintenance runs about 4 to 5 hours. Micro loc reties run 1 to 3 hours depending on how overdue you are.

items.q: Can I wash my locs right after interlocking?
items.a: Yes. Interlocking locs are secure from the moment they leave the chair. Wait 24 hours if you want to be cautious, then wash normally with a residue-free shampoo.

items.q: Do I need to grow my locs out to interlock?
items.a: No. Interlocking works on locs of any length. Longer locs take more time per visit but the technique is the same.

items.q: Can I comb my interlocking locs out someday?
items.a: Very difficult. Interlocking creates a much tighter loc structure than palm rolling, so takedowns become impractical quickly. If reversing your locs is a possibility, palm rolling is a better long-term choice.

items.q: Do you interlock for men?
items.a: Yes. Interlocking services are offered for all clients regardless of gender. Same pricing, same technique.

items.q: What if I have not interlocked in six months?
items.a: Book the consultation, not the maintenance. Overdue interlocking usually needs separation work and a plan before we can start regular maintenance again.
